literal: every year and you are safe
usage: This is the most common all-purpose greeting in the Levant for birthdays and holidays. While the literal translation '3eed meelaad sa3eed' is understood, locals heavily prefer this phrase or '3a2bal el miyyeh' (may you reach 100). It requires gender and number agreement based on who you are addressing.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when wishing a happy birthday to a woman or girl.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use this when addressing multiple people celebrating together.

variants.label: common alternative
variants.note: A very common birthday-specific wish often said immediately after the main greeting.

variants.label: literal translation
variants.note: The literal translation of 'happy birthday', often used in writing, on cakes, or in formal contexts.

responses.english: And you are safe (replying to a man)
And you are safe (replying to a woman)
May you be kept safe (general thank you)

examples.arabic: كل سنة وإنت سالم يا أحمد، عقبال المية!
examples.transliteration: kull saneh w inta salem ya ahmad, 3a2bal el miyyeh!
examples.english: Happy birthday Ahmad, may you reach 100!

examples.arabic: اليوم عيد ميلادها، لازم نقول لها كل سنة وإنتي سالمة.
examples.transliteration: el yom 3eed meelaadha, lazem n2oul laha kull saneh w inti salmeh.
examples.english: Today is her birthday, we have to wish her a happy birthday.

examples.arabic: شكرا على الهدية، وأنتو سالمين يا رب.
examples.transliteration: shukran 3ala el hadiyyeh, w intu salmeen ya rabb.
examples.english: Thank you for the gift, and may you all be well.
